Marcus, Rafael —

Thanks for looping me in. I pulled together the technical artifacts and a concise explanation below to help your auditors evaluate the variance.

How our log retention & targeted deletion works (summary):
- Inference serving emits two primary streams: audit/event logs (persisted to long-term object storage) and ephemeral inference traces / KV cache state (kept in GPU-backed TTL caches and not eligible for customer-scoped retention changes).
- Persisted logs are sharded by tenant-id and log-category. We maintain per-object metadata including creation_time, tenant_id, category, and a deletion_digest (SHA256) computed at write time.
- A scoped-variance is implemented by registering a tenant + category allowlist. Our deletion pipeline then targets objects matching that allowlist for scheduled retention-based deletion. Deletions are recorded in an immutable deletion ledger with entries: object_key, deletion_time, operator_id, deletion_digest.

Evidence we can provide:
- CAIQ mapping (see attached caiq-mapping-v1.pdf) that points to our control IDs where deletion and immutable ledger are described.
- Sample deletion report (attached sample-delete-report.csv): includes object_key, tenant_id, category, created_at, deleted_at, deletion_digest. We sanitize object_key values for auditor review.
- Audit trail: we can provide the immutable ledger extract for a scoped timeframe (PDF) and an HMAC-signed index proving ledger integrity.

Operational/controls proposal for a 180-day variance:
1) Allowlist: Greenline will provide explicit tenant_id and category names.
2) Contract addendum: include variance clause plus requirement for quarterly attestation from Greenline confirming continued need. Karhtik to draft.
3) Extra controls: enable KMS key scoping for those stored objects and increase retention of access logs to 2 years.
4) Canary run: we propose a 30-day canary where we apply the variance to a synthetic tenant (or a narrow subset) and produce the full deletion ledger for review.

Limitations/risks:
- We cannot apply the variance retroactively to objects already moved to cold archive in certain regions without a manual restore; we'll document any gaps in the example report.
- Ephemeral caches are outside scope and will continue to be pruned per standard TTLs.

I'll prepare the immutable ledger extract and a sanitized ledger HMAC proof for the canary run. Rafael — once you get sign-off from Marcus, I'll coordinate the canary and delivery schedule.
